Write me a 3 paragraph story about a tiger who learns to cook biryani
9:46 AM

Raja and the midnight biryani

Raja, a broad-striped tiger of Ranthambore, had one secret: he was bored of hunting. One winter night he wandered near the forest guard's hut and caught a smell so rich with cloves and fried onions that his whiskers trembled. Through the window he saw a steaming pot of biryani, and from that moment deer held no charm for him.

Learning was harder than stalking. He traded a peacock three shiny feathers for a stolen recipe page, borrowed a dented pot from an abandoned campsite, and lit his first fire by accident. His rice turned to paste, his onions turned to coal, and once he mistook cardamom for pebbles and spat them across the clearing. The langurs kept score of his failures on a tree trunk, but Raja simply washed the pot in the river and began again.

On the twentieth try, he sealed the pot with dough, let it sit on slow embers, and waited with a patience no hunt had ever taught him. When he lifted the lid, the steam rolled out soft and golden, every grain standing separate. The langurs came down quietly, the peacock brought his whole family, and even the old sloth bear asked for seconds. From then on, the jungle feared Raja a little less and visited him a lot more, always around dinner time.
